ruling.explanation:
To both parties. Trip TRP-02804 (27 Aug 2026, Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres to Blk 25 Ghim Moh Link), charged SGD 45.82.

1) Deviation. On the governing GPS trace (EV-GPS-02804, weight 1.0) the driven route measures 29.13 km against the booked optimal of 22.1 km (EV-TRIP-02804). POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure, not the rounded trip-record copy. Excess = 7.03 km, 31.8%. That clears both establishment gates (over 0.8 km and over 20%), so the deviation is established; but it fails both materiality gates (8.0 km and 50%), so it is not a material deviation. The repeat-deviation check is therefore not engaged, and in any event EV-DPROF-02804 shows deviation_flags_90d = 1 against 329 completed trips, far below POL-RD-06's tests, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. Both advocates agree on this, and I accept it.

2) The driver's traffic excuse. The driver says traffic was heavy so he took another road. POL-RD-13 tests that assertion against the trip's traffic advisory, and the only advisory, EV-ADVIS-02804-01, is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run. The driver's own statement names no evidence ID for any advisory; under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction. The driver's brief argues that because the driver 'cites' the missing identifier the case must escalate. I reject that: the citation to EV-ADVIS-02804-01 appears only in the advocate's argument, not in the driver's own assertion, and POL-RD-13(1) turns on the asserting party's own naming of an evidence ID. The traffic excuse accordingly carries no weight under POL-RD-08, the deviation stands at the measured figure, and the case does not escalate.

3) Other exculpatory routes are closed. POL-RD-04 cannot run (EV-CHAT-02804 holds 0 messages, so no rider instruction and no waypoint_hint). POL-RD-05 cannot run (no amendment timestamps; amended_optimal_distance_km is null). POL-RD-12 does not apply (vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL).

4) No escalation trigger fires. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (100% coverage, 229 fixes at a 10 s interval, max_gap_sec 0.0), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; trip identifiers and timestamps agree; the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 and charged-total ceilings; and every fare line has a counterpart on the trace or trip record.

5) The refund. fare_model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 22.1 + 0.28 x 29.8) x 1.2 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.50 on-optimal-route ERP = 36.7628. Refund = charged_total 45.82 - 36.7628 = 9.0572, rounded UP to SGD 9.10. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 19.8% of the amount charged, below the 90% share that would make it a full refund, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 9.10. (The rider contested SGD 8.50; the arithmetic yields SGD 9.10.)

6) ERP. The single SGD 1.50 charge for PIE Eunos westbound is on the optimal route and matched to the trace (nearest fix 35.3 m, inside the 250 m crossing radius), so there is no billing-integrity finding and no POL-RD-09(4) referral. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended in the recomputed fare and is not added on top.

Confidence: every artifact carrying the deciding facts (EV-GPS-02804, EV-TRIP-02804, EV-FARE-02804) is at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. Confidence is 0.95.

Execution: the monetary effect of SGD 9.10 exceeds the POL-GEN-05 threshold of SGD 8.00, so the ruling issues but the amount is held for release by a human reviewer. This is a provisional ruling; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
